messages:
Asha (support): FYI customer 'AcmeMail' on Dedicated-VPC hitting intermittent 401s when users SSO via company IdP. Error appears after ~30s of idle time. Repro attached.

Dana (cust-prod): Repro steps: 1) Login via SSO -> get signed_session cookie. 2) CALL API /v1/generate with Cookie header (no Authorization). 3) Some requests succeed, others 401 with 'missing auth header'. Token present in X-Auth-Bearer on backend. Happens only via our L7 (HAProxy) in front of istio.

Ben (eng-infra): Can you paste the raw headers from a failing request? Any load balancer rewrite rules? Also, which gateway: istio-ingressgateway or internal L7? :thinking_face: 

Asha (support): failing curl -v captured from customer (sanitized):

```
> GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.dedicated.acme
> Cookie: _sso=eyJhbGciOiJ...
> User-Agent: curl/7.68.0
> Accept: */*
< HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
< content-type: application/json
< x-request-id: r-1234
```

But on the backend trace we see `X-Auth-Bearer: bearer abc.def.ghi` for the same request. Backend code rejects because Authorization header missing. Looks like LB is moving Authorization -> X-Auth-Bearer but istio is checking Authorization and returning 401 before app sees X-Auth. Hypothesis: Istio ext-authz uses Authorization but LB strips it and inserts X-Auth-Bearer; when route takes a direct path to envoy it's missing.

Carl (eng-runtime): This rings a bell — we had a previous bug where keep-alive + connection reuse could drop Authorization during proxy->envoy header normalization. Can you check if `proxy_protocol` is enabled and if HAProxy has `http-request set-header Authorization %[req.hdr(X-Auth-Bearer)]` rules? If HAProxy rewrites to X-Auth and not Authorization, ext-authz (pre-filter) will 401.

Dana (cust-prod): HAProxy config snippet from customer:
```
http-request del-header Authorization
http-request set-header X-Auth-Bearer %[req.cook(_sso)]
```
They do delete Authorization and set X-Auth-Bearer. They expected istio to forward X-Auth-Bearer to the app which would exchange it, but istio ext-authz runs earlier.

Ben (eng-infra): Ok that explains it. Two options: 1) Have HAProxy set Authorization instead of X-Auth-Bearer (preserve header name). 2) Configure istio ext-authz to accept X-Auth-Bearer (requires change in our ext-authz policy mapping). For immediate mitigation ask customer to stop deleting Authorization. 

Asha (support): Customer tried setting `http-request set-header Authorization 'Bearer %{+Q}[req.cook(_sso)]'` but still seeing failures intermittently. Any ideas?

Carl (eng-runtime): Intermittent suggests header duplication/race. If both HAProxy and internal LB add headers, they may get concatenated or one gets truncated depending on header normalization. Can you ask for tcpdump on sidecar to show raw headers for failing vs succeeding requests? Specifically look for repeated Authorization headers or extremely long header values.

Ben (eng-infra): Also check envoy header size limits and `forward-client-cert` settings. If the header becomes >8KB Envoy might truncate and drop tokens.

Asha (support): Next steps agreed:
- Ask customer to switch to setting Authorization directly and remove del-header Authorization (temp rollback) ✅
- Request tcpdump from istio sidecar of a failing request (we'll provide pcap filter) ✅
- If reproduced, patch istio ext-authz mapping to accept X-Auth-Bearer OR add HAProxy rewrite rule to set Authorization consistently. 

deploy-bot: scheduled run: authz-policy-reload on staging at 2026-03-18T02:00Z :white_check_mark:

Dana (cust-prod): thanks all, providing pcap now. Appreciate quick turnaround :pray:
